overview: Medford municipal and school officials joined the local state legislative delegation for the 8th Annual Legislative Forum at the West Medford Community Center to answer constituent questions on transportation, housing, aging, charter review, and municipal staffing.

items.title: Welcome and Introductions
items.summary: Poet Laureate and Elder Services Director Terry E. Carter opened the forum, introduced attending state and local officials, and recited an original poem.

items.title: West Medford Community Center Access Walkway Project
items.summary: Officials provided an update on $350,000 secured through state and ARPA funding for the long-delayed DCR rear access walkway project, noting the project is out for bid and a $50,000 operational appropriation is planned in the upcoming state budget.

items.title: Condominium Conversion and Housing Affordability
items.summary: Councilor Collins addressed resident concerns regarding housing displacement, explaining that the City Council is in early development of a condominium conversion ordinance to regulate rental conversions and support the Affordable Housing Trust.

items.title: MBTA Transit Service and Station Accessibility
items.summary: Elected officials discussed systemic issues across the MBTA, addressing bus route reductions, driver shortages, service issues with The RIDE, state revenue from the Fair Share Amendment, and ADA accessibility concerns at local commuter rail stations.

items.title: Aging Population, Healthcare Workforce, and Fiscal Capacity
items.summary: Participants discussed city and state challenges regarding the aging population, highlighting healthcare and elder care workforce shortages, senior housing needs, and the city's overall budgetary and revenue constraints.

items.title: City Charter Review and Mayoral Term Length
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn and Charter Study Committee members described the ongoing review of the city charter and announced an upcoming public information session scheduled for June 8.

items.title: Diversification of School and Municipal Workforce
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent and municipal officials detailed initiatives to recruit and retain diverse educators and city staff, while school committee members noted recent substantial salary increases for district paraprofessionals amid broader funding constraints.

items.title: Community Announcements and Closing
items.summary: Terry Carter announced the upcoming April 15 citywide cleanup and adjourned the forum.
